answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on shared work, with voting weight capped per task and rewards delayed until independent reviewers confirm the result. If a cluster of fake identities coordinates to approve bad work, evidence of collusion lets the system slash their deposits, while honest reviewers retain theirs. Spreading identities across dawn, dune, and knoll does not help: each still needs capital at risk, so a sybil attack becomes costly rather than free.
